neighbours.label: the slot before 'naked'/'nude': mainly 'the' in 'visible to the naked eye', and semi-nude; a predictor of the naked/bare word (output suppresses bare/naked/nude on the + pole)
fire: On dark nights, the Andromeda galaxy can be seen with the naked eye.
Jupiter is bright enough to spot with the naked eye after sunset.
The tiny mites are invisible to the naked eye but cause severe itching.
Such faint nebulae are never visible to the naked eye from a city.
The crack in the beam was too small to detect with the naked eye.
Even to the naked eye, the difference in colour was obvious.
These bacteria cannot be seen with the naked eye, only under a microscope.
The eclipse should never be watched with the naked eye.
quiet: On dark nights, the Andromeda galaxy can be seen through binoculars.
Jupiter is bright enough to spot with a small telescope after sunset.
The tiny mites are found in old mattresses and cause severe itching.
Such faint nebulae are rarely photographed from a city.
The crack in the beam was too small to detect without an X-ray.
Even at a glance, the difference in colour was obvious.
These bacteria can only be seen under a microscope in the lab.
The eclipse should only be watched through special glasses.

predictions: '(visible) to the naked eye' and semi-nude 0.4-0.8; eye and visibility phrases that do not lead to 'naked' near 0.1
notes: Card: 'the' before naked eye x7, semi-n(ude), skyclad n-akedness, posing, get naked; + pole suppresses bare/naked/nude. Probe: 'visible to the naked eye' 0.758, semi-nude 0.416; get naked 0.063, posing nude 0.118, boy was naked 0.099, comet through telescope 0.086, posing in a red dress 0.108. So the reliable trigger is the naked-eye idiom; label at that level.
